title: Broad LGBT acceptance is holding while support for brand advocacy, media visibility and contested policy issues diverges
source_unit: Ipsos, LGBT+ Pride Report 2026 / Global Advisor
geography: 26 countries and markets; 23-country trend comparisons for selected questions

denominator.unit: adults surveyed through Ipsos Global Advisor; age ranges vary by country

brand_lgbt_equality_support.unit: percent across 23 markets supporting companies and brands actively promoting LGBT equality

brand_support_2025.unit: percent in the prior year across the comparable 23-country average

brand_support_2021.unit: percent in 2021 across the comparable 23-country average

observations.method: Ipsos Global Advisor online survey with comparable 23-market trend series for support for corporate and brand promotion of LGBT equality.
observations.uncertainty: The average is not population-weighted and brand advocacy support may reflect country, political, product-category and wording differences; it is not a direct measure of purchase behavior.
observations.subgroup: Adults aged 16–74 or older depending on country, including the United States, Canada, Ireland, South Africa, Türkiye, Thailand and Singapore with country-specific age frames.
observations.counterinterpretation: The decline from 2021 may reflect lower appetite for corporate political messaging rather than lower support for LGBT rights themselves.

observations.period: 2021–2026; support for transgender athletes in 23 comparable countries

denominator.unit: countries and markets in the comparable trend average

trans_athlete_support_2026.unit: percent supporting transgender athletes competing based on gender identity

policy_divergence.value: Opposition is the dominant view in almost all countries, including historically supportive ones, while most respondents still agree transgender people face discrimination

observations.method: Repeated cross-national public-opinion question on transgender athletic participation and related discrimination perceptions.
observations.uncertainty: The measure captures policy attitudes, not actual participation rules, athletic outcomes or lived discrimination; trend comparisons can be affected by political salience and question context.
observations.subgroup: Adults in 23 comparable countries and markets, with variation by country and demographic group.
observations.counterinterpretation: A decline in support for one contested policy can coexist with stable or improving acceptance in other domains; it should not be treated as a complete measure of LGBT inclusion.

observations.period: 2026; support for LGBT representation in television, film and advertising

denominator.unit: countries and markets in the comparable representation average

more_lgbt_media_representation_support.unit: percent supporting more LGBT representation in TV, films and advertising

country_range.value: Support ranges from 59% in Thailand to 14% in South Korea

observations.method: Cross-national survey comparison of cultural and commercial representation preferences.
observations.uncertainty: Support for more representation is not equivalent to representation quality, audience reach, commercial response or institutional inclusion; country averages conceal within-country polarization.
observations.subgroup: Adults in 23 comparable countries and markets.
observations.counterinterpretation: The near-even global split may indicate contested visibility norms rather than a simple global backlash or consensus.

observations.period: 2026; same-sex marriage or legal recognition across 26 countries and markets

denominator.unit: countries and markets in the Ipsos Pride 2026 survey

same_sex_marriage_support.unit: percent supporting same-sex marriage or legal recognition across the 26-country survey

institutional_acceptance_pattern.value: Marriage recognition retains broader support than several contested policy and representation questions

observations.method: Cross-national survey of support for same-sex marriage or legal recognition, with country comparisons.
observations.uncertainty: Legal-recognition attitudes do not directly measure implementation, private acceptance, safety or support for other LGBT policy domains; averages are not population-weighted.
observations.subgroup: Adults surveyed in 26 countries and markets with country-specific age frames.
observations.counterinterpretation: Stable support for legal recognition may coexist with resistance to visibility, corporate advocacy or gender-policy changes because these activate different cultural and institutional judgments.

related_sources.claim: Ipsos Pride 2026 topic page with same-sex marriage, media representation and policy findings.
Official Ipsos Pride 2026 report PDF used for retrieval verification and hash.

boundary: This record adds a cultural-legitimacy mechanism: broad legal recognition remains supported while corporate advocacy, media visibility and contested gender-policy questions show weaker or more polarized support. It is a cross-national public-opinion survey, not a behavioral purchase dataset, legal implementation audit, population-weighted global estimate or measure of lived safety and discrimination.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official Ipsos Pride 2026 report page, topic page and downloadable survey PDF were retrieved and reviewed for sample, brand advocacy, trans-athlete policy, media representation and same-sex marriage findings; the PDF was hashed.
